title: Key and chord detection from songs
question: Why the key detector fails, and how to detect key, chords and notes from songs (imported or playing live) in the browser and put them on the project.
bottomLine: The key label bug is small: projectKey() only reads melody tracks and falls back to a fake 'detected A minor'. Fix it to read all pitched tracks, show confidence and a second guess, and say 'no key yet' when unsure. Key and chords from an imported song can be done in plain JS with our own FFT (beat-aligned chroma, EDM key profiles, chord templates with Viterbi smoothing), no download: expect about 60-65% exact key on club tracks (Mixed In Key about 89-94%; most misses are relative or fifth swaps) and about 71-79% chord accuracy (best neural about 81-85%), good enough for an editable chord lane. Note-level transcription needs Basic Pitch (Apache-2.0, about 1 MB) and only works well on stems, so it pairs with SE-6. Spotify no longer gives key data to new apps. Key and chords are fine copyright-wise; copying a song's melody note for note is the risk.
findings: Mixed In Key leads key detection: 89% overall and 94% on club tracks in Dubspot's 2026 200-track test; KeyFinder 76%, rekordbox 69%, Beatport tags 60%. Errors cluster on relative major/minor and fifths, which still mix harmonically.
Classic profile matching on audio chroma gets about 30% exact on the GiantSteps EDM set; EDM-tuned profiles (Faraldo, CC BY paper) get 58-64%. Profiles are genre-specific.

Logic Pro 12 Chord ID (Jan 2026, improved in 12.3) fills a Chord Track from audio; reviewers report 85-95% on pop and electronic but about 30% fixes on dense mixes. Studio One has Detect Chords; Ableton converts harmony to MIDI notes (best on isolated parts); FL Studio 2026 detects chords only from MIDI.
Chordify and Moises analyse ahead and show chords synced with playback (Moises: easy/medium/advanced detail). Chord ai does live mic chords offline with a scroll-back timeline.
Live chord readouts need about 0.5-1 s of audio per decision; Basic Pitch cannot run in real time (CQT needs more than 1 s, about 120 ms model delay, non-causal decoding).

Licences: Essentia.js is AGPL, libKeyFinder GPL-3, Chordino GPL-2, madmom models CC BY-NC-SA: not usable in our shipped file. Basic Pitch (Apache-2.0), Meyda, tonal.js and web-audio-beat-detector (MIT) are fine.
Basic Pitch: under 17K parameters, about 0.3 MB ONNX or about 1 MB TF.js weights, about 60 ms per 2 s window on WASM (about 5-6 s for 3 minutes); good on single lines, rough on full mixes.
Spotify closed Audio Features (key, mode, tempo) and 30-second previews to new apps on 27 Nov 2024.
Chordify's position: chord progressions aren't protected, unlike lyrics or melody; it retracts songs on request. Melody copied note for note is the clear risk.
'Camelot' is a registered Mixed In Key trademark (a further filing, CAMELOT WHEEL for music software, Oct 2025); rekordbox calls its codes 'Alphanumeric' and Traktor uses 'Open Key'.
recommendations: SE-7a (S, bug; sound-engine-dev + studio-ux-dev): detectKey over all pitched tracks with bass and downbeat weighting, confidence plus a second-guess key, a relative-key tie-break, null when there are too few notes, and an honest #keyInfo label that can be locked with a tap.

SE-7b (M; sound-engine-dev): analyseAudio(buf) in plain JS (Worker or chunked, cached): bpm, beats, downbeat, key with confidence and a second guess, chords per bar. Runs on SE-6 stems when present; AI-3 consumes it.
SE-7c (M; studio-ux-dev + assistant-dev): editable chord strip, PROJ.chords that all generators follow, and voice actions: what key is this, take the chords from this song, match a loop to my key.
Later (M, after SE-6): notes from a stem with Basic Pitch behind the same opt-in model download; only for the user's own audio or a stem they choose.
Later (M): live listen mode from the mic with a current-chord readout and 'keep the last 8 bars'; needs owner UX approval as a new mic mode.

ideas.name: What key is this?
ideas.hook: Drop any song or loop and say 'Keys, what key is this?': it answers by voice with key, bpm and how sure it is, and sets the project on yes.
ideas.loop: drop audio > spoken key and bpm > set project > build parts in key
ideas.why: The most common producer question when sampling or remixing; a voice answer with honest confidence beats a bare tag.
ideas.risks: Relative-key errors on vocal-heavy or modal tracks; mitigated by confidence and a one-tap fix.
ideas.similar: Mixed In Key; Moises Key Detector; rekordbox key analysis

ideas.name: Take the chords
ideas.hook: 'Keys, use the chords from this song': a chord lane appears and every new pad, bass and pluck follows it, in our own voicings.
ideas.loop: reference song > chord lane > generate parts on it > tweak chords by tap
ideas.why: It is Logic 12's headline feature, now in a browser and driven by voice; it builds on AI-3's reference track.
ideas.risks: About 25% chord errors on dense mixes; better on SE-6 stems; needs a beat grid.
ideas.similar: Logic Pro 12 Chord ID; Studio One Chord Track; Chordify

ideas.name: Play it in my key
ideas.hook: Drop a sample or loop: Keys detects its key and shifts it to the song's key (nearest of plus or minus 6 semitones).
ideas.loop: drop loop > detect > transpose > in key
ideas.why: Ableton's Splice browser plays samples 'in key with your Set'; producers expect this now.
ideas.reuse: Key detection plus the existing pitch or playback-rate path
ideas.risks: Pitch-shift quality on drums or vocals; offer resample versus keep-length options.
ideas.similar: Ableton Live 12 with Splice; Splice Bridge

ideas.name: Listen mode
ideas.hook: Hold the phone up to a song in the room: it shows the chord now plus the last 8 bars, then 'keep these chords'.
ideas.loop: listen > see chords live > keep > build on them
ideas.why: Captures inspiration from a club or radio moment, like Chord ai, but straight into a project.
ideas.risks: Weak bass on laptop and phone mics, room noise; label it rough; owner rules on the mic apply.
